summary: Completed packet 53 by reusing the existing Rust shell, Trunk bundle host and owned Chromium fixture. crates/web/src/startup.rs initializes GPUI Kit, embeds its font and icons, and opens one canvas window; shell.rs owns transient session/check/retry state. Same-origin Fetch and the existing IndexedDB binding select the host-owned HttpOnly session through browser_session::Sessions and resolve_session -> account::resolve_on; no bearer enters the wasm application and no second authentication mechanism or database migration was added. Stock Kit Button supplies the required interaction; no new custom control was needed. Retained the existing shared-control wasm clock adaptation. Added a crate-local nightly toolchain pin and stronger cookie, transport, runtime-error and asset-header assertions. Preserved unrelated existing edits, including coordinator runner changes and Android work. Only the affected workflow row and this handoff were changed as documentation. Coordinator follow-up: the development runbook's root wasm build example needs an explicit nightly selector; the protected runbook was not edited in this packet.

Initial focused baseline: cargo test --locked -p boardcraft-mobile-edit-host --features web-smoke --test web_shell -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture passed all 3 cases, with 0 ignored/filtered, against the disposable rustday_test database.

Diagnostic: cargo build --locked -p boardcraft-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown on the root stable toolchain failed with E0554 in wasm_thread 0.3.3. This is an upstream nightly requirement, not a missing target. The web-local toolchain pin makes Trunk select the supported toolchain without a hidden test-only version override; explicit root wasm commands must use +nightly-2026-10-31.

Final focused suite: cargo test --locked -p boardcraft-mobile-edit-host --features web-smoke --lib --test web_shell -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture passed 1 asset unit test and all 3 browser cases, with 0 ignored/filtered, in 39.70 seconds for the browser suite. Its Trunk subprocess successfully built the actual development bundle using the web-local toolchain selection.

web_shell_loads_and_resolves_session passed: an owned headless Chromium profile mounts exactly one nonzero canvas, renders the unauthenticated shell without a session request, resolves a real browser session and renders the signed-in shell across reload. Fresh PostgreSQL connections independently confirm the same account/session verifier, with no extra login or session issuance. Cookie metadata asserts HttpOnly, exact host, API path and Strict same-site policy without logging credential values.

web_shell_handles_unavailable_and_rejected_session passed: a real account_sessions table lock yields HTTP 503; checking/unavailable frames contain no stale signed-in content. Tab/Enter activates the stock Retry connection button and resolves the unchanged session after rollback. Independently deleting that session yields HTTP 401, removes the origin binding, renders the unauthenticated shell, and makes the next reload issue no resolve request. Every session identity check reconnects to PostgreSQL.

web_shell_serves_cross_origin_isolation passed: actual Trunk HTML, generated JavaScript module and wasm responses carry COOP same-origin and COEP require-corp, with the expected module/wasm MIME types. The module instantiates and the shell renders under a secure, crossOriginIsolated loopback origin. The existing /preview/ JavaScript page still returns successfully.

Database boundary assertions passed inside both focused browser runs: cargo tree --locked -p boardcraft-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown excludes postgres, tokio-postgres, windows and boardcraft-desktop. Chromium and its driver receive no database credentials. Final journeys assert only the expected same-origin session Fetch traffic, no external resource requests, no WebSocket/WebTransport connections and no unexpected browser runtime exceptions; the wasm application has no direct PostgreSQL transport.

web_assets::tests::bundle_snapshot_cannot_serve_later_filesystem_edits passed: changing an accepted file after startup does not change served bytes, a subsequently added credentials file is not exposed, and reloading a bundle containing that unsupported file is rejected.

Development bundle measured from the final Trunk output: 133259110 bytes total (about 127.1 MiB), comprising wasm 133063227, generated JavaScript 190452, bootstrap HTML 975 and font license 4456 bytes. The font and loading icon are embedded in wasm; dist output is ignored. No release/compressed bundle was measured.

Signed-in reload observations were 1417, 1830 and 1900 ms including OCR. These are local development observations/upper bounds, not exact first-paint timestamps or production performance claims.
